motivation: The native motor listens to a public tariff but weakly selects according to what it knows. A bilateral evidence input at the 4000-step screening point yielded only small selection gains. The previous identity and marker results suggest testing how the measurement is spatially bound to the action it concerns.
fixed_inputs: Same six-component physically updated, taste-gated sensory trace and same one trainable zero-initialized gain as the bilateral evidence arm. Same exact 8000-step ticket parents, all support and cost schedules, native 20-node motor, optimizer and update count. The true ticket location is already displayed by its visual mark.
intervention: Bilateral reference supplies k*coverage in the second coordinate to both sides. Offer-local supplies sqrt(2)*k*coverage only on the visibly marked ticket side. Opposite supplies the same current on the pass side. Detached supplies the same current on a random side independent of the actual ticket side. For a given k and coverage all conditions have identical extra squared signal energy. No threshold, correct buy flag, or probability-to-motor mapping is provided. Native motor chooses in all arms. The tariff remains identically displayed in all conditions.
verification: Stage-zero actions/earned outcomes must agree bitwise across arms. Compare 8000-step endpoints on new common geometries with physical known/novel/unfed histories, tariff-matched cross-history randomization and action-only transplants of the evidence trace. Check whether correctly binding to either stable side, versus a randomly moving signal, is enough; fixed opposite is an informative control, not another unknown-target label. Evaluate long-stream and near-neighbor stress on the fixed endpoints. Both 6-birth cohorts; no choose-best-root reporting.
